C. Speech Interference Levels. Background noise above certain levels interferes with one's ability to understand oral communication. The following figure illustrates some current knowledge of this phenomenon.
Figure 2 - Voice level and distance between talker and listener for satisfactory face-to-face speech communications as limited by ambient noise. Along the abscissa is the A-weighted sound level meter reading (dB(A)).
(SIL-Past, Present, and Future, J. C. Webster, Sound and Vibration, August, 1969)
